content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] driver and a [product_name] panel [product_name]. My issue seems simple, but I’m unable to solve it and need some help. I want to know how these devices can be connected. Is it enough to set their addresses like: driver: 192.168.0.1, panel: 192.168.0.2? Do I need to do anything else? The program is running and the [product_name] screen displays as expected, but the [product_name] panel remains in Offline mode. Apologies for my English.

Additionally, you need to specify the correct [product_name]-IP in the panel or, if already listed, select the IP address. This allows the panel to identify which [product_name] it should communicate with. Go to the panel main menu > [product_name] Selection.

Hi, also verify that the message text is enabled for the panel. Open the message text properties and ensure the option to display the message on the panel (enable [product_name] TD and/or Both) screen is checked. Hope this helps.

To summarize: IP address 192.168.0.1 for the driver, 192.168.0.2 for the panel. Message text option "both" highlighted. 192.168.0.1 entered in [product_name] Selection on the panel, but it's still not working. For further information, when accessing [product_name] settings: PanelMainMenu -> Network -> IP Address, the screen shows "Failed to submit".

Hi, check the panel settings. The panel has its own IP address, but it also needs to know which [product_name] IP to connect to. Refer to Appendix "D" in the [document]. It contains all menu screens and setup instructions. Hope this helps.
A new question by [user_name] has been opened in a separate thread about changing the delay time on the panel not affecting the [product_name]. Best regards [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The user is struggling to establish communication between two [product_name] devices, each with distinct IP addresses. Even after configuring device settings and message text options, the panel remains offline, providing unhelpful error messages. The process lacks clear step-by-step instructions and effective troubleshooting feedback from the interface.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects an easy and direct setup for IP communication between the devices using menu configuration, without needing advanced troubleshooting. They also expect the interface to deliver clear and meaningful error feedback to guide resolution.
